title: Asking for Directions
summary: A visitor asks for directions to a community centre, checks the route and practises explaining it.
description: An A2 listening lesson about asking for, following and checking directions in a town centre, with landmarks, distance expressions and clarification questions.
levelRationale: A2 learners can follow a short sequence of familiar directions, understand landmarks and distances, and use clarification questions. The route requires sequencing rather than only locating one explicit fact.

context.setting: A visitor meets a local near the town library and needs to reach the community centre before a class starts.
context.estimatedDuration: 12–15 minutes; editorial estimate for preparation, two listens, route checking and pair practice.

objectives: Identify the destination, starting point and approximate travel time after the first listen.
Sequence a route using landmarks, turns and distance expressions after a second listen.
Ask for clarification and give a short route using polite questions, imperatives and checking phrases.

preListening: Look at library, pharmacy, bridge and community centre. Predict which landmarks could help someone find a place.
Match go past, cross, at the roundabout, on your right and about five minutes to their meanings.
Predict one polite question for checking a direction.
global: Listen once and choose the best summary: A) A visitor asks how to reach a community centre and checks the route. B) A visitor books a hotel room. C) Two people plan a bus journey.
Note the destination and approximate walking time.
detailed: Complete the route: start at the ____, go past the ____, cross the ____, and turn left at the ____.
Put these in order: turn left at the roundabout; walk past the pharmacy; cross the small bridge; leave the library.
Which phrase checks the final location? What is next to the community centre?
Decide true or false: the route takes about five minutes; the centre is on the right; Maya crosses the main road.
extension: In pairs, draw a four-landmark map. One student asks for a destination; the other gives three or four steps. The listener checks one detail with Is it…? or Do I…? Then swap roles.
Challenge: give directions without naming the destination until the partner identifies it from the landmarks.

transcript.text: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the community centre?
Yes, I am. I am near the town library.
Then leave the library by the main entrance and go straight on for about two minutes.
Do I go past the pharmacy?
Yes. Walk past the pharmacy and cross the small bridge.
The bridge next to the park?
Exactly. After the bridge, continue to the roundabout and take the second exit.
Turn left at the roundabout. The community centre is on your right, next to the sports hall.
So it takes about five minutes from the library, right?
That is right. You cannot miss it.

answerKey.answer: A; the destination is the community centre and the route takes about five minutes.
answerKey.explanation: Maya asks for the community centre and Leo gives a walking route with a time estimate.
The route starts at the library, passes the pharmacy, crosses the bridge and continues to the roundabout.

answerKey.answer: leave the library; walk past the pharmacy; cross the bridge; take the second exit and turn left
answerKey.explanation: The instructions appear in that sequence in lines 4, 6, 8 and 10.

answerKey.answer: Maya asks The bridge next to the park?; the sports hall is next to the centre.
answerKey.explanation: Maya checks which bridge Leo means, and Leo identifies the neighbouring sports hall.
The journey takes about five minutes and the centre is on the right. Leo says to cross the small bridge, not the main road.

procedure: Preparation (3 minutes): sketch four landmarks and activate go straight, past, cross and turn left.
First listen (2 minutes): play without the transcript; learners choose the summary and note destination and time.
Second listen (4 minutes): learners complete and order the route; pause only after the first attempt if needed.
Feedback (3 minutes): reconstruct the route and ask learners to point to lines proving each answer.
Speaking extension (5 minutes): pairs use a map, ask for a destination and check one detail.
differentiation: Support: provide a labelled map and replay lines 4–10 once.
Stretch: remove two labels and ask for a different starting point plus one clarification question.
followUp: Learners write four directions from the classroom to a familiar place, underline sequence words and exchange instructions to check the route.

vocabulary.definition: continue beyond a place without stopping there
go from one side of a road or bridge to the other
leave a roundabout using its second road
the place is easy to see or find

dialogue.text: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the community centre?
Yes, I am. I am near the town library.
Then leave the library by the main entrance and go straight on for about two minutes.

Yes. Walk past the pharmacy and cross the small bridge.
The bridge next to the park?
Exactly. After the bridge, continue to the roundabout and take the second exit.
Turn left at the roundabout. The community centre is on your right, next to the sports hall.
So it takes about five minutes from the library, right?
That is right. You cannot miss it.

questions.q: What is next to the community centre?

trueFalse.statement: The route takes about five minutes from the library.
trueFalse.explanation: Maya checks the time in line 11 and Leo confirms it in line 12.

trueFalse.statement: Maya should take the first exit at the roundabout.
trueFalse.explanation: Leo tells her to take the second exit in line 8.

teacherTips: Use a simple labelled map to connect direction phrases to movement and landmarks.
Practise Is it…? and Then what? before the second listen.
During pair work, focus on route order and intelligibility rather than correcting every article or preposition.

es.title: Pedir indicaciones
es.summary: Una visitante pregunta cómo llegar a un centro comunitario, comprueba la ruta y practica cómo explicarla.
es.description: Una lección A2 sobre pedir, seguir y comprobar indicaciones en el centro de una ciudad, con lugares de referencia, distancias y preguntas para pedir aclaraciones.
es.levelRationale: El nivel A2 es adecuado porque el alumnado sigue una secuencia breve de indicaciones, comprende lugares de referencia y distancias, y usa preguntas de aclaración.

context.setting: Una visitante se encuentra con una persona de la zona cerca de la biblioteca y necesita llegar a un centro comunitario antes de una clase.
context.estimatedDuration: 12–15 minutos; estimación editorial para la preparación, dos escuchas, la comprobación de la ruta y la práctica en parejas.

objectives: Identificar el destino, el punto de partida y el tiempo aproximado tras la primera escucha.
Ordenar la ruta usando lugares de referencia, giros y distancias tras la segunda escucha.
Pedir aclaraciones y dar una ruta breve mediante preguntas corteses, imperativos y expresiones de comprobación.

preListening: Observen biblioteca, farmacia, puente y centro comunitario. Predigan cuáles ayudan a encontrar un lugar.
Relacionen go past, cross, at the roundabout, on your right y about five minutes con su significado.
Predigan una pregunta cortés para comprobar una indicación.
global: Escuchen una vez y elijan: A) Una visitante pregunta cómo llegar a un centro comunitario y comprueba la ruta. B) Reserva un hotel. C) Planea un viaje en autobús.
Anoten el destino y el tiempo aproximado a pie.
detailed: Completen: salen de la ____, pasan por la ____, cruzan el ____ y giran en la ____.
Ordenen: girar en la rotonda; pasar por la farmacia; cruzar el puente; salir de la biblioteca.
¿Qué frase comprueba la ubicación final? ¿Qué lugar está junto al centro?
Decidan si son verdaderas: la ruta dura cinco minutos; el centro está a la derecha; cruza la carretera principal.
extension: En parejas, dibujen un mapa con cuatro lugares. Una persona pide un destino y la otra da tres o cuatro pasos; quien escucha comprueba un detalle con Is it…? o Do I…?. Después cambien los papeles.
Para ampliar, den indicaciones sin decir el destino hasta que el compañero lo identifique.

procedure: Preparación (3 minutos): dibuje cuatro lugares y active go straight, past, cross y turn left.
Primera escucha (2 minutos): reproduzca sin transcripción; anoten destino y tiempo.
Segunda escucha (4 minutos): completen y ordenen la ruta; pause si hace falta.
Corrección (3 minutos): reconstruya la ruta y pidan señalar las líneas que prueban cada respuesta.
Extensión (5 minutos): las parejas usan un mapa, piden un destino y comprueban un detalle.
differentiation: Apoyo: entregue un mapa rotulado y repita las líneas 4–10 una vez.
Ampliación: quite dos rótulos y pida usar otro punto de partida y una pregunta de aclaración.
followUp: Escriban cuatro indicaciones desde el aula hasta un lugar conocido, subrayen los conectores e intercambien las instrucciones para comprobar la ruta.

vocabulary.definition: cruzar al otro lado de una calle o puente
tomar la segunda salida de una rotonda
es fácil de ver o encontrar

trueFalse.statement: La ruta dura unos cinco minutos desde la biblioteca.
trueFalse.explanation: Maya comprueba el tiempo en la línea 11 y Leo lo confirma en la línea 12.

trueFalse.statement: Maya debe tomar la primera salida.
trueFalse.explanation: Leo indica que tome la segunda salida en la línea 8.

teacherTips: Use un mapa sencillo para relacionar las expresiones con el movimiento y los lugares.
Practique Is it…? y Then what? antes de la segunda escucha.
Observe el orden de la ruta y la inteligibilidad sin corregir cada artículo o preposición.
